To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Tonga plate is separated from the India plate by a NW-SE trending transform fault, the Lau Ridge is a remnant of the Tonga plate that has been separated from the India and Pacific plates, and the Lau Basin is an oceanic basin with an average elevation more 3,000 meters above the deep Pacific.

(1) the Lau Basin, which separates the Tonga and the Lau Ridges, was formed by the intrusion of basalt and the separation of the two ridges, and that (2) the Lau Ridge and the Tonga Ridge are not the same ridge but are separated by the Lau Basin.

the Lau Basin is the result of a 300 km long transform fault separating the Tonga plate from the India plate and that the basin is a product of the intrusion of hot material from below the Tonga plate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the tectonic evolution of the Lau Basin and its relation to the Tonga Trough, Lau Ridge, and Tonga Ridge.
the tectonic evolution of a small plate (the Tonga plate) that is being subducted beneath the Tonga Ridge.
the processes of crustal formation, deformation, and destruction in a region of complex plate interactions, the western Pacific.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Lau Basin is an oceanic basin, and the Tonga and Kermadec ridges are the active volcanic arc and trench system of the subduction zone between the India plate, the Tongan plate, and the Pacific plate.
the Lau Basin, a small oceanic basin, is a region where two plates are separating, with the India plate being the larger of the two.
the Tonga and Kermadec Trenches are the sites of subduction of the Pacific Plate beneath the Tonga Plate, which is moving in an approximately N-S direction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Lau Basin is the site of active spreading between the Tonga plate and a small plate, which is in turn being subducted beneath the Tonga Ridge.
the Tonga and Fiji arcs are the result of subduction and the Tonga Ridge the result of spreading.

the Tonga and Kermadec trenches, and the Tonga-Kermadec and Lau ridges, are all parts of one large arc system which has been formed by the interaction of the Pacific, Australia-Indian, and Tonga plates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a new plate in the Pacific Ocean.
the Tonga-Lau region is an example of a complex tectonic setting where the plate boundaries are not obvious and where there is an absence of sediment.
there is a new plate, the Tongan plate, between the Pacific and Indian plates and that the Tonga Trough and the Lau Basin are the sites of the plate boundary between these two plates.
